**2012 · Storage plus partial readout · supporting**
$V_{\rm recall}=2DT+V_{\rm readout}$
$J_{\rm obs}=\alpha J$
$L_{\rm obs}^*=L^*/\sqrt\alpha$
$V_{\rm ideal,obs}(\infty)=\sqrt{2D/(\alpha J)}$
$V_{\rm recall}(T,L)\ge2DT+\sqrt{2D/J}$
before: Missing spikes reduces readout information while the full circuit keeps diffusing at the same $D$. Reading becomes slower and less precise. A selected fraction of neurons need not carry the same fraction of information; $\alpha J$ follows from random spike thinning or a verified information fraction. The general ideal total-error limit is $2DT+\sqrt{2D/J}$; it equals $2D(T+\tau)$ only at equality in the information bound. [Why printed Eq. 6 needs this qualification](../chapters/ch-memory-readout.html#sec-memory-fig3-and-caution).
after: Missing spikes reduces readout information while the full circuit keeps diffusing at the same $D$. Reading becomes slower and less precise. A selected fraction of neurons need not carry the same fraction of information; $\alpha J$ follows from random spike thinning or a verified information fraction. With full spike access, the ideal total-error limit is $2DT+\sqrt{2D/J}$; it equals $2D(T+\tau)$ only at equality in the information bound. [Why printed Eq. 6 needs this qualification](../chapters/ch-memory-readout.html#sec-memory-fig3-and-caution).

**2025 · Universal size laws · central approximation**
$\Pr(s>S)\simeq e^{-\beta S^{2/d}}$
$\beta=\dfrac{q^2}{2\ell_c^2v_d^{2/d}}$
$(v_1,v_2,v_3)=(2,\pi,4\pi/3)$
before: At large positive $q$, a typical counted field surrounds one nearly quadratic peak: radius $r_*\simeq\ell_c\sqrt{2\epsilon/q}$ for peak excess $\epsilon$. The scaled excess $q\epsilon$ tends to a unit-mean exponential law. Substitute size $s=v_dr_*^d$. [Chapter 11; Eq. 1, Methods S4 and corrected constants](../chapters/ch-place-sizes.html#sec-place-size-law).
after: For a smooth stationary isotropic Gaussian map at large positive $q$, a typical counted field surrounds one nearly quadratic peak: radius $r_*\simeq\ell_c\sqrt{2\epsilon/q}$ for peak excess $\epsilon$. The scaled excess $q\epsilon$ tends to a unit-mean exponential law. Substitute size $s=v_dr_*^d$. [Chapter 11; Eq. 1, Methods S4 and corrected constants](../chapters/ch-place-sizes.html#sec-place-size-law).
